title: Make stock CPU profiles portable
summary: Make the active m68k CPU and complete rumiga-core graph compile under no_std plus alloc for bare-metal 32-bit RISC-V while isolating the host-only FPU implementation.

risk.failure_mode: Cargo feature unification or incorrect F-line fallback could reintroduce std into firmware builds or change stock CPU exception behavior.
risk.rollback: Revert the M1-002 CPU, core feature forwarding, portable profile, CI, and documentation commits together to restore the previous host-only CPU graph.

compatibility.detail: Default desktop consumers retain std and FPU behavior; consumers disabling m68k defaults must now select exactly one runtime profile, and FPU remains unavailable under no_std.

security.detail: No network, credential, authorization, media, persistence, unsafe-code, or FFI policy changes.

tests.proves: The active integer CPU implementation compiles without std as an optimized bare-metal 32-bit RISC-V artifact.
The complete stock Amiga core dependency graph, including m68k, compiles for the pinned bare-metal target.
Valid std and no_std CPU profiles pass, invalid combinations fail with stable diagnostics, Line-F fallback is preserved, and the default FPU-enabled workspace remains green.
Repository-owned declarative profiles enforce the foundation and optimized stock-core RISC-V builds.

evidence.location: Pending hosted M1-002 pull-request and final main promotion evidence
evidence.proves: Linux, macOS, bare-metal RISC-V, governance, and the strict aggregate validate the promoted CPU portability contract from clean revisions.
